London: School of Oriental and African Studies. 306 pp. (publication of the 1984 University of London PhD 'A comparative-historical study of the Manenguba languages'; reissued London: Routledge 2012, doi:10.4324/9780203045930, ISBN 9781136349119)
tone_statements.quote: Phonetically, there are level and contour tones or tone glides. There is downdrift, which means that when a H follows a L, the H is always lower than a H which precedes the L. … This means that phonologically there are only H and L tones which follow each other. … A H becomes downstepped high (*H) after H and before pause … The second explanation of the "mid” tone is that it is due to the loss of L between two H tones. … There are falling and rising contour tones … The first is interpreted as a combination of H + L, the second as L + H.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones, H and L, in the Manenguba languages incl. Akoose; falling/rising glides analysed as H+L, L+H; downdrift, downstepped H (also lexicalised), floating L in prefixes; stress unsettled.

sources.citation: Ekanjume, Beatrice. 2008. The phonological phrase as a prosodic domain in Akóóse. Journal of West African Languages 35(1-2): 57ff. (open access, JWAL site)
sources.quote: p. 60: 'we find the nouns featuring with the following tones: a high tone, a low tone, a low-high tone, a high and low tone, a low and low tone, and a low and high tone in the root ... The initial vowel of one of the adjectives (like most initial vowels in Akóóse) is toneless ... it gets its tone from default Low at the postlexical level.' Rules found (p. 66): high tone spreading, vowel deletion, vowel shortening, vowel insertion, tone docking, default Low. No mention of stress or accent as a property of Akoose anywhere in the article (the only 'stress' strings are in titles of cited works).
sources.locator: printed p. 60 (p. 4), section 1 data discussion; conclusions p. 66-67
sources.note: Only open-access modern prosody paper on Akoose; downloaded now; describes root tone patterns (H, L, LH, HL..), toneless prefixes with default L, HTS and tone docking; no stress/accent -- corroborates the tonal coding.
